correctness.rationale: For all integer \(n\ge3\), count synchronized CCA configurations via the published Theorem 3 irrotationality condition. The discrete 1-form has unique signed differences in \(\{-1,0,1\}\). Its zero circulations are equivalent to normalized 1-Lipschitz integer heights, with exactly three global colors. Column vertical differences d in \(\{-1,0,1\}\) and horizontal step a in \(\{-1,0,1\}\) give a 3-by-3 Laurent transfer; the cyclic trace and \(z^0\) condition enforce both horizontal closing relations. The characteristic polynomial factors as \((\lambda-s)(\lambda^2-(3+2s)\lambda+s^2+s-2)\). Its unique dominant Fourier value \((7+\sqrt{33})/2\) has variance \(5/4-19\sqrt{33}/132\), giving the \(n^{-1/2}\) Laplace coefficient. Open-ladder Perron projection yields the claimed ratio. Direct trajectory simulation and independent face/basis circulation enumeration agree with transfer for all 597780 states at \(n=3,4,5,6\); exact determinant tests and longer transfer coefficients passed. An additional direct comparison checks open-ladder colorings for \(2\le n\le6\). Finite tests are corroboration, not proof of the all-\(n\) statement.

value.rationale: The exact size and leading asymptotic of the synchronization basin under random starts are natural infinite-family dynamical quantities. The universal prior criterion neither evaluates the basin nor isolates the global winding constraint. The explicit spectral exponential constant, sharp Gaussian correction and cyclic versus open ladder \(n^{-1/2}\) ratio reveal an interpretable topological mechanism relevant to finite cyclic-network reliability. Not a routine single-size table or merely relabelled existing theorem.
